# Citations

All sources used in the Temporal workflow orchestration evaluation for the
personal AI-assisted engineering assistant. Numbered sequentially; referenced
as `[N]` throughout the analysis and reference files.

---

**[1]** "temporalio/temporal." *GitHub*, accessed 2026-04-07.
<https://github.com/temporalio/temporal>
**Tier:** 2
Data extracted: 19.4k stars, 1.5k forks, MIT license, Go 99.5%, v1.30.3
(April 1, 2026), 160 releases, 8,757 commits. Forked from Uber's Cadence.

**[2]** "Self-hosted guide — Deployment." *Temporal Documentation*, accessed
2026-04-07.
<https://docs.temporal.io/self-hosted-guide/deployment>
**Tier:** 2
Data extracted: Docker Compose setup via samples-server repo, PostgreSQL +
Elasticsearch default, gRPC port 7233, Web UI port 8233, binary deployment
option, systemd/Nginx tutorials referenced.

**[3]** "Schedules." *Temporal Documentation*, accessed 2026-04-07.
<https://docs.temporal.io/schedule>
**Tier:** 2
Data extracted: Schedule spec format (interval, calendar, cron_string),
timezone handling (default UTC, IANA names), overlap policies (Skip default,
BufferOne, BufferAll, CancelOther, TerminateOther, AllowAll), pause/unpause,
backfill, catchup window (default 1 year), pause-on-failure, action limits,
result passing between runs (2 MiB limit).

**[4]** "Retry Policies." *Temporal Encyclopedia*, accessed 2026-04-07.
<https://docs.temporal.io/encyclopedia/retry-policies>
**Tier:** 2
Data extracted: Default retry policy — 1s initial interval, 2.0 backoff
coefficient, 100s maximum interval, unlimited maximum attempts. Activities
retry by default; workflows do not. Formula: min(initial × coefficient^attempt,
max_interval). Non-retryable error types. Schedule-to-Close timeout limits
total retry duration for activities.

**[5]** "Workflow Message Passing." *Temporal Encyclopedia*, accessed
2026-04-07.
<https://docs.temporal.io/encyclopedia/workflow-message-passing>
**Tier:** 2
Data extracted: Three message types — Signals (async write, fire-and-forget),
Queries (sync read, no history impact), Updates (sync write with response).
Workflows as "stateful web services."

**[6]** "Data Encryption." *Temporal Documentation*, accessed 2026-04-07.
<https://docs.temporal.io/production-deployment/data-encryption>
**Tier:** 2
Data extracted: Codec Server architecture (independent HTTP server), payload
encryption via Payload Codec (byte-to-byte), encrypted data covers workflow/
activity I/O, signals, memos, headers. Decoded payloads client-side only.
POST /decode and /encode endpoints. CORS required. Key management
infrastructure needed.

**[7]** "Temporal CLI." *Temporal Documentation*, accessed 2026-04-07.
<https://docs.temporal.io/cli>
**Tier:** 2
Data extracted: `temporal server start-dev` for local dev server (in-memory
SQLite, Web UI at localhost:8233, gRPC at localhost:7233). `--db-filename`
for persistent SQLite. Command groups: activity, batch, env, operator,
schedule, server, task-queue, workflow. Environment variables:
TEMPORAL_ADDRESS, TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE, TEMPORAL_API_KEY, TEMPORAL_TLS_CERT,
TEMPORAL_TLS_KEY.

**[8]** "Temporal Cloud Pricing." *Temporal*, accessed 2026-04-07.
<https://temporal.io/pricing>
**Tier:** 2
Data extracted: Essentials $100/mo (1M actions), Business $500/mo (2.5M
actions), Enterprise contact (10M actions). Overage: $50/M first 5M, scaling
down to $25/M over 200M. Active storage $0.042/GBh, retained $0.00105/GBh.
$1,000 free credits for new users. Startup program $6,000 credits.

**[9]** "Sending Messages." *Temporal Documentation*, accessed 2026-04-07.
<https://docs.temporal.io/sending-messages>
**Tier:** 2
Data extracted: Signal-With-Start pattern (lazy initialization — starts
workflow if not running, then signals it). Update-With-Start (combines
init + update in single roundtrip, not atomic). Signals from any Client,
CLI, or workflow-to-workflow. executeUpdate vs startUpdate methods.

**[10]** "Scaling Temporal: The Basics." *Temporal Blog*, accessed
2026-04-07.
<https://temporal.io/blog/scaling-temporal-the-basics>
**Tier:** 2
Data extracted: Load testing with MySQL (4 CPU, 32GB RAM). Per-service
baseline: 1 CPU, 1GB RAM. 150→1,350 state transitions/sec via optimization.
History shards: dev default 4, production recommended 512, max 4,096.
Shard count immutable after creation. 512 shards → History pods need 8GB RAM.
Database CPU is primary scaling constraint (target <80%).

**[11]** "Security Controls." *Temporal Documentation*, accessed 2026-04-07.
<https://docs.temporal.io/best-practices/security-controls>
**Tier:** 2
Data extracted: Namespace isolation (logically segregated, no cross-namespace
interaction by default). Service accounts for non-human access with separate
API keys. mTLS for gRPC endpoints. API key rotation every 90 days minimum.
SAML 2.0 SSO. Client-side encryption via custom codecs. Failure Converters
for encrypting error messages.

**[12]** "Web UI." *Temporal Documentation*, accessed 2026-04-07.
<https://docs.temporal.io/web-ui>
**Tier:** 2
Data extracted: Debugging features — Event History views (Timeline, Compact,
All, JSON), ~40 event types, input/output inspection, workflow control
(cancel, signal, update, reset, terminate). Filterable by status, workflow
ID, type, time ranges. Saved views (up to 20). Task failure monitoring
(flags after 5 consecutive failures). Downloadable JSON history. Parent/child
tree view.

**[13]** "Activity Execution." *Temporal Documentation*, accessed
2026-04-07.
<https://docs.temporal.io/activity-execution>
**Tier:** 2
Data extracted: Activities as units of work with customizable timeouts and
retry policies. "Activity Task either runs or timeouts." Heartbeat mechanism
for cancellation. Asynchronous completion pattern. Activity IDs unique within
open activities of a single Workflow Run.

**[14]** "Cron Jobs." *Temporal Documentation*, accessed 2026-04-07.
<https://docs.temporal.io/cron-job>
**Tier:** 2
Data extracted: Classic 5-field cron format, predefined shortcuts (@yearly,
@monthly, @weekly, @daily, @hourly, @every). UTC default, CRON_TZ prefix
for custom timezones (v1.15+). DST caveats (may run 0, 1, or 2 times).
Recommendation to use Schedules instead.

**[15]** "Namespaces." *Temporal Documentation*, accessed 2026-04-07.
<https://docs.temporal.io/namespaces>
**Tier:** 2
Data extracted: Namespace as unit of isolation. Unique Workflow ID per
namespace. Heavy traffic isolation between namespaces. Default namespace
"default." Single namespace is still multi-tenant. Settings (retention,
archival) per namespace. Zero code changes for self-hosted→Cloud migration.

**[16]** "Archival." *Temporal Self-hosted Guide*, accessed 2026-04-07.
<https://docs.temporal.io/self-hosted-guide/archival>
**Tier:** 2
Data extracted: Backs up closed workflow histories to blob storage (S3, GCS,
local filesystem for testing). Asynchronous after close (up to 5 min delay).
Experimental feature, not subject to normal versioning/support. Disabled by
default. Unsupported via Docker. URI immutable after namespace creation.
